executableEvidence.originalDotnetStartupRed: FAIL: startupFailed=False, remoteEvaluations=1; expected true and zero.
executableEvidence.dotnet: Three real-SDK/synthetic-transport scenarios passed, including document failure with a successful remote endpoint, local hot-path evaluation, Details, logging, and blocked requests.
executableEvidence.angular: Twenty TypeScript/service cases passed, including degraded payloads, identity changes, pending-refresh expiry, read-time TTL after a previous positive read, authorization failures, owner-safe provider teardown, and SSR state isolation.
executableEvidence.structure: English text, frontmatter, local links/anchors, PowerShell labels/syntax, and support-file checks passed.

initialFindings: Angular computed cached a positive decision after TTL when no reactive dependency changed.
The global browser provider retained a closure to a destroyed service.
focusedCodeReview.redEvidence: Three new regression tests failed: browser cached TTL, SSR cached TTL, and releasing the owned global provider. The replacement-owner test already passed.
corrections: Use an uncached decision accessor that reads the state signal and checks current time on every invocation.
Retain the provider instance; on browser teardown, replace its binding with NOOP_PROVIDER only if its metadata object is still the active owner.
focusedCodeReview.greenEvidence: All twenty Angular cases and all three .NET scenarios passed after both corrections.
focusedCodeReview.scope: The reviewer did not rerun the corrected implementation; regression results are the post-fix evidence.

limitations: The guided responses were reasoned implementations, not individually compiled generated applications.
The control/guided comparison is a small diagnostic sample, not a statistical reliability benchmark.
A focused scenario was rerun after the final wording refinement; the entire five-sample comparison was not repeated.
No target business application, real identity flow, rendered Angular template, live BFF, live browser provider, or cloud deployment was certified.
The pinned .NET native SDK still lacks a deterministic polling teardown contract; the harness exits its process.
